what: gp_lanes_check.c, -std=c11 -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno, clang and gcc: the lane kernels (gp_lanes_pair.inc, gp_lanes_query.inc) against the PR818 fork's scalar kernels (gp_scalar.inc: gp_extract.py's verbatim copy of wedge_ill_conditioned, wedge_precise_forward/backward, gp_pair_forward/backward, gp_query_unit, gp_query_contract_pair, gp_query_contract_vjp from the level-2 build's query_guard_compact.c; GP_RANK 22, GP_PROJECTOR 0, GP_SYMMETRIC 0, the study's -D values), every output -- the features, both adjoints, the query contraction and its two adjoints -- byte for byte over ROWS*6 rows in groups of sixteen of each kind (uniform; u and v near parallel, which the scalar kernel sends to its FP64 fallback; tiny; zero u; large; sparse), the flagged rows recomputed by the scalar kernel; then each kernel's ns a row, the scalar kernel row by row and the lanes a group at a time with their transposes, on uniform rows -- 1,008 rows (every operand L2-resident) and 24,576 (the features streaming to memory); parts: gp_parts.c, the lane forward's parts on one group of sixteen rows held in L1, 20,000 times, TSC cycles (2.3 GHz) a row

prefetch.what: gp_pf_bench.c (GP-PF-0): the lane forward a group at a time over ROWS rows whose outputs were made cold (64 MiB written between rounds), without and with the next group's input and output rows prefetched -- the overlay's tasks prefetch so -- and the scalar kernel row by row; every feature byte for byte; ns a row, median of 9 rounds

tasks.what: gp_tasks_check.c: each fork's geometric-head entries from the build without the lanes and with them, each library loaded on its own, on the same inputs -- row counts 1, 15, 16, 17, 66, 111, 512, 1,024 (rows past the last group of sixteen), serially and on a four-thread pool, every batch's first row with a zero prefix and every seventh near parallel to its own (the FP64 fallback among the lanes) -- every output byte for byte

LN1.what: the forward normalises in float (the scalar kernel rounds o*inv from double)

LN2.what: a row the scalar kernel sends to its FP64 fallback kept as the lanes computed it

LN3.what: the backward's rows past the last group of sixteen start one row late

LN4.what: the query contraction's output a rounded float sum with a term the scalar kernel lacks

LN5.what: one adjoint's first term scaled by 1 + 2^-23 after it lands

LE1.what: the norm's square and sum fused: od*od of a widened float is exact in double (48 significant bits), so one rounding of od*od+norm is the two roundings' value

LE2.what: the query pair's two updates swapped: acc[k] and acc[i] are distinct accumulators (i < k)

LE3.what: the vjp's dot accumulated on every lane: a lane whose norm is at most the epsilon never reads it
